claims.text: The proposed family of fairness regularizers for linear and logistic regression is convex.
Any constant regressor exactly minimizes all of the proposed fairness regularizers.
Building separate regression models for each group does not substantially improve the accuracy-fairness trade-off on most evaluated datasets out-of-sample compared to single models.
Individual fairness is generally more costly in terms of accuracy loss than group fairness across most studied datasets.

evidence.description: Since these loss functions and our fairness regularizer are convex, the combined objective functions obtained from our framework are also convex, and thus permit efficient optimization.
We note that any constant regressor (any w such that w · x = c for all x in X and some c in R) exactly minimizes all of our fairness regularizers.

Perhaps surprisingly, building separate models for each population barely improves the trade-off (and in some cases, hurts the trade-off for some values of lambda) across almost all datasets and fairness regularizers.

Individual fairness appears to be strictly more costly than group fairness for the entire regime between the extremes of lambda = 0 and lambda -> infinity for a majority of these datasets (with the exception of COMPAS and Default datasets).

methodologies.name: Convex Fairness Regularization Framework
methodologies.description: An optimization framework adding convex fairness regularizers (individual, group, or hybrid) to MSE or log-loss objectives for linear and logistic regression models.
conditions: Single model vs. separate group models comparison

limitations.text: Most prior work on machine learning fairness focuses on binary classification rather than regression settings with continuous targets.
Evaluating equality of odds empirically for regression models is difficult because true labels may appear only once in dataset samples.
Group fairness regularizers and separate models are more prone to overfitting than individual fairness and single models, requiring larger L2 regularization parameters.
Linear models perform poorly on certain tasks like the Default dataset.
The detailed trade-off between accuracy and fairness is strongly domain-dependent and lacks prescriptive universal patterns across datasets.
